raw_response:
I'm 68 years old now, been farming this same piece of land for 25 years. My wife and I, just the two of us, we've got 4.5 mu in Quzhou. Our son works in the factory in Handan, so it's mostly me doing the field work, though my wife helps with sowing and cooking meals when I'm busy. My legs aren't what they used to be, but I still know every corner of these fields.

We've always done wheat-maize double cropping. That's our living. We need the wheat for our own flour, and the maize we sell. With only 4.5 mu and just two of us, every yuan counts. I don't have money to waste on fancy things.

**Winter wheat this year:** I'll plant around October 12th, same as always. My neighbor Old Wang says the Jimai variety is doing well, so I'll buy that from the seed shop in town — about 35 yuan per mu. I used to save my own seed, but the shop seed gives better yield, and at my age I need every extra jin I can get.

For fertilizer, I bought three bags of compound fertilizer for the whole plot. That works out to about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I put most of it down before planting, and in spring if the wheat looks a bit yellow at jointing, I'll topdress a little urea — maybe another 3-4 kg per mu. The extension guy last year said I should use more, but fertilizer is expensive and I need to keep some cash for my wife's medicine. My neighbor uses about the same and does fine.

I'll irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings, once in March at green-up, and once at heading if it's dry. Pumping water costs money — about 40 yuan each time for electricity — but wheat needs water. Last year I only did twice and the yield was down, so I'll stick with three.

For pests, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring. If I see aphids, I'll spray insecticide, but I'll wait and see first. No point spending money before I need to.

I'll hire Lao Zhang's tractor to plow and prepare the seedbed. I don't have my own tractor anymore — sold it five years ago when my knees got bad. That costs me about 100 yuan total. For harvest in June, I'll hire the combine harvester that comes through the village. My wife and I will do the sowing and fertilizing ourselves.

**Summer maize:** As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I need to get the maize in the ground. The window is tight — sometimes only four or five days. I'll buy hybrid seed from the shop, about 55 yuan per mu. With maize you can't save seed, everyone knows that.

For maize fertilizer, I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 10 kg of nitrogen per mu. One application is enough for maize — no time for split dressing with the double crop, and anyway I'm not sure it helps much. Old Wang next door does it all at once and his maize is always good.

I'll irrigate twice for maize: once if it's dry right after planting to get it germinated, and once at tasseling in August. If the summer rains are good, maybe I skip the first one. Water bills add up, and maize can handle a bit of dry better than wheat.

I'll spray herbicide once after planting to keep the weeds down. Maize grows fast if you keep the weeds out.

Tillage between wheat and maize? No time for deep plowing. I'll just run Lao Zhang's rotary tiller quickly and plant the same day or next day. Sometimes I plant without tilling if the wheat stubble isn't too thick, but this year I'll do a light till.

Labor is mostly me and my wife. For wheat, we'll spend about 8 family days total — sowing, fertilizing, irrigating, watching the fields. For maize, about 7 family days. I might hire one day of help during wheat harvest if my back is acting up, and maybe one day for maize sowing if the window is too tight. Hired labor is 100-120 yuan per day now, so I try to avoid it.

Yield? If the weather cooperates, I expect about 380 kg per mu of wheat and about 420 kg per mu of maize. Last year was a bit dry and I got 350 and 400, so I'm hoping for a little better. But I don't count on it until it's in the bag.
